sentences.text: Lonchodectes is a genus of reptile and pterosaur from the Late Cretaceous of England, primarily found near Kent.
This animal possessed long jaws with many short teeth that were compressed vertically, resembling a pair of sugar tongs.
Researchers suggest that Lonchodectes compressirostris likely had crests on its lower jaws, similar to related species.
David Unwin estimated a maximum wingspan of nearly 2 meters for this generalist species, comparing it to a gull.
Recent studies suggest that Lonchodectes had limb proportions similar to azdarchids and may have lived in a similar way.
The genus Lonchodectes was named by Hooley in 1914 based on a partial upper jaw fossil found in the Upper Cretaceous Upper Chalk near Kent.

The type species Lonchodectes compressirostris was originally named in 1851, transferred to another genus in 1870, and finally established as the type species of Lonchodectes in 1914, with 9 recorded fossil occurrences known today.

In 2003, the genus was placed in the family Lonchodectidae within Ctenochasmatoidea, and later in 2006, it was placed within Azhdarchoidea, though it also belongs to the parent group Ornithocheiroidea.
Recent reviews have limited the genus Lonchodectes to only its type species, L. compressirostris.

It is debated whether Lonchodectes is a valid genus, as species were previously assigned to Ornithocheirus until the work of David Unwin, and the status of L. platystomus is debated, with some suggesting it may belong to the genus Amblydectes. Most potential species of Lonchodectes are known only from fragmentary remains and have undergone multiple generic reassignments.
